# Fracture Surgery
Simple, compound and shattered fractures are all set surgically. On an [bold]arm, hand, leg or foot[/bold] you only need to open the incision. On the [bold]chest or head[/bold] you also need to open the bone cavity, and close it again at the end. For how to tell fractures apart and what to do after, see [textlink="Fractures" link="CMUGuideMedicalBones"].
Fractures on limbs can be set on yourself.
## Set Simple Fracture 1. [italic]Open the incision.[/italic] (Chest or head: also open the bone cavity.)
2. Realign the fracture with a [bold]bone setter[/bold].
3. Apply [bold]bone gel[/bold].
4. [italic]Close up.[/italic] (Chest or head: close the bone cavity.)
## Set Compound Fracture 1. [italic]Open the incision.[/italic] (Chest or head: also open the bone cavity.)
2. Realign the compound fracture with a [bold]bone setter[/bold].
3. Apply [bold]bone gel[/bold].
4. [italic]Close up.[/italic] (Chest or head: close the bone cavity.)
## Set Shattered Fracture A shattered bone needs a [bold]bone graft[/bold] to hold it together. 1. [italic]Open the incision.[/italic] (Chest or head: also open the bone cavity.)
2. Realign the shattered fracture with a [bold]bone setter[/bold].
3. Apply [bold]bone gel[/bold].
4. Insert a [bold]bone graft[/bold].
5. Set the grafted bone in place with the [bold]bone setter[/bold].
6. [italic]Close up.[/italic] (Chest or head: close the bone cavity.)
## Afterwards Put a cast on the limb within 5 minutes of setting it, or the bone may heal crooked.
